note: Unit 12 assignment tasks in plain language, based on the Pearson BTEC First ICT Unit 12 specification and the centre scheme of work (three assignments). Used by the Assignment guide, the Assignment builder and the AI assignment coach. The teacher's official brief and client always take priority.

assignments.title: Assignment 1: Characteristics and uses of software programs
assignments.scenario: You are on work experience at a software development company. Your line manager gives you two simple programs the company has written and asks you to explain how they work and comment on their quality, before you are trusted to write code for a client. Your teacher supplies the two programs and the official brief.
assignments.evidence: A report on the two programs (with annotated code and a flowchart)

tasks.title: Explain the purpose and characteristics of two programs
tasks.asks: For each of the two simple programs, explain what it is for (its purpose) and its characteristics: the type of language, its inputs, processing and outputs, and the tools and techniques it uses (command words, subroutines, string handling, file handling, data structures, event handling, selection, loops, variables and data types). Level 1 (1A.1) only needs you to identify these; Level 2 Pass needs you to explain them.
checklist: The purpose of each program is explained in your own words
Inputs, processing and outputs are identified for each program
The type of programming language is stated (e.g. event-driven Visual Basic) with a reason
Each construct or technique used is named AND you explain what it does in that program
You refer to specific lines or parts of the code (annotated screenshots help)
You have run the programs (or dry-run them with a trace table) and say what happens
It is written in your own words

tasks.title: Comment on quality, suggest improvements and draw a flowchart
tasks.asks: Choose one of the programs and comment on its quality using the quality measures (efficiency, maintainability, portability, reliability, robustness, usability). Suggest improvements, and provide a flowchart showing how the program would process data once your improvements were made.
checklist: Each quality measure is covered with evidence from the code (not general statements)
Weaknesses are identified, e.g. no validation, unclear names, repeated code, no comments
Each improvement is specific and linked to the weakness it fixes
The flowchart uses the correct symbols (start/end, input/output, process, decision)
The flowchart shows the improved processing, including any new validation or decisions
The flowchart has been checked with test values (a dry run)

tasks.title: Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of the program
tasks.asks: Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of the software program in a balanced way, considering its purpose, its users and the quality of its design and code, and reach a conclusion about how good it is.
checklist: Strengths AND weaknesses are both covered, with evidence from the code
Points are linked to the program’s purpose and its users
Quality measures are used to structure the discussion
You weigh up which strengths and weaknesses matter most, and why
You reach a supported overall conclusion

assignments.title: Assignment 2: Design, develop and test a software program
assignments.scenario: A client has given your company a brief describing a problem that a software program could solve, such as replacing a paper-based booking or ordering system. You will design the program, develop it in Visual Basic (or the language your teacher sets), and test and refine it. Your teacher gives you the official brief with the client’s requirements.
assignments.evidence: Design documents, the working program (source code with comments and an executable), a completed test plan with screenshots, a feedback and changes log

tasks.title: Describe the purpose and user requirements
tasks.asks: Show that you understand the brief: describe the intended purpose of the program and the user requirements. Level 1 identifies them; Level 2 describes them in detail.
checklist: The intended purpose is described in your own words (not copied from the brief)
Every user requirement from the brief is listed
Each requirement is described: what it means and why the user needs it
You identify who the users are
It is presented clearly and professionally, as a report for the client

tasks.title: Produce a design for the program
tasks.asks: Produce a design including a problem definition statement, a proposed solution (main tasks with inputs and outputs, screen layouts and navigation, algorithms in pseudocode or flowcharts, data structures and storage, validation), a list of any predefined functions/subroutines with sources, and a test plan.
checklist: A problem definition statement describes the current problem and how the program will solve it
The main program tasks are described with inputs, processing and outputs
Screen layouts are annotated (every control labelled with its type and purpose)
A navigation diagram shows how the screens link
Algorithms are shown as pseudocode and/or flowcharts
Data structures, data storage and validation are planned
Predefined functions/subroutines are listed with their sources
A test plan lists tests, test data and expected results

tasks.title: Produce a detailed design with alternatives
tasks.asks: Produce a detailed design that includes alternative solutions, a detailed proposed solution using a range of design tools, and test data.
checklist: At least two alternative solutions are shown (e.g. two screen layouts or two algorithms)
The differences between alternatives are explained
The proposed solution uses a range of tools: IPO table, annotated layouts, navigation diagram, pseudocode/flowcharts, data design
Control structures, validation and error handling are planned in detail
Test data covers normal, boundary and erroneous values for each input

tasks.title: Justify the design decisions
tasks.asks: Justify your design decisions, including how they will fulfil the stated purpose and user requirements, and any design constraints.
checklist: Each major decision (layout, navigation, data structures, validation, algorithms) is justified
Justifications link back to specific user requirements and the purpose
You explain why the chosen alternative is better than the others
Constraints (language, time, device capabilities) are identified and you explain how they shaped the design

tasks.title: Develop the program
tasks.asks: Develop a program for the brief which includes a user interface (input and output), constructs and techniques, and commentary (comments) throughout the code. Level 1 is developed with guidance.
checklist: The program has a user interface with clear inputs and outputs
It uses a range of constructs: variables and data types, selection, iteration, subroutines
It uses techniques such as string handling, file handling, arrays/records and event handling where the brief needs them
Comments explain what each part of the code does
Controls and variables have meaningful names
The program has been compiled into an executable
Any predefined code is acknowledged in comments

tasks.title: Develop a functional program that meets the brief
tasks.asks: Develop a fully functional program that meets the given brief.
checklist: Every user requirement in the brief is implemented
The program runs without crashing for normal use
Input is validated and errors are handled with helpful messages
Calculations and outputs are correct (checked by testing)
Data is stored and retrieved correctly where required

tasks.title: Test for functionality and repair faults
tasks.asks: Test the program for functionality using the test plan and against the original requirements, and repair any faults.
checklist: Every test in the test plan has been carried out
Actual results and pass/fail are recorded for each test
Screenshots provide evidence of the tests
The program is checked against each original requirement
Faults are repaired and the failed tests are re-run
The repairs are recorded (what was wrong and how it was fixed)

tasks.title: Gather feedback and use it to improve
tasks.asks: Test the program using the test data, gather feedback from others on the usability and quality of the program, and use it to improve the software program. Repair any faults.
checklist: Feedback is gathered from real users or others (e.g. a questionnaire or interview)
Feedback covers usability and quality (reliability, efficiency, maintainability, portability)
The feedback is recorded with who gave it
Changes made because of feedback are described and re-tested
Faults found are repaired

tasks.title: Refine the program using code quality and feedback
tasks.asks: Refine the software program, taking account of the quality of the code and user feedback.
checklist: The code is reviewed for quality: names, comments, structure, repetition, efficiency
Refinements improve code quality (e.g. subroutines instead of repeated code, constants, better validation)
Refinements respond to user feedback
Each refinement is explained and justified
The refined program is re-tested and still meets the requirements
Design documents are updated to match the final program

assignments.title: Assignment 3: Review the finished software program
assignments.scenario: The client wants to know how well the program you developed in Assignment 2 meets their needs before it is used every day. Your teacher gives you the official brief and the format (a report or a presentation).
assignments.evidence: A review report or presentation, with evidence from testing and feedback

tasks.title: Explain how the program is suitable for the requirements and purpose
tasks.asks: For the software program, explain how the final program is suitable for the original requirements and purpose. Level 1 identifies how; Level 2 explains.
checklist: Each original requirement is listed with how the program meets it
Fitness for purpose is explained: does it solve the client’s problem?
Evidence is given (test results, screenshots)
It is written in your own words, for the client

tasks.title: Review the extent to which requirements are met
tasks.asks: Review the extent to which the software program meets the original requirements, considering feedback from others and any constraints.
checklist: You judge how far each requirement is met (fully, partly, not met) with reasons
User feedback is used as evidence
User experience (ease of navigation, clarity) is reviewed
Constraints are discussed: how they affected the program and how you worked around them
Quality is reviewed using the quality measures

tasks.title: Evaluate against designs and code quality, and recommend improvements
tasks.asks: Evaluate the final software program against the initial designs and the quality of the code, justify any changes made, and make recommendations for further improvement.
checklist: The final program is compared with the initial design, element by element
Every change from the design is identified and justified
The quality of the code is evaluated with examples
Strengths and weaknesses are weighed to reach supported conclusions
Recommendations for further improvement are specific and justified
